articles.summary: Senate races in Georgia , Kansas and South Carolina were reclassified with a nudge toward Democrats in the latest analysis from the closely watched Cook Political Report. The latest: In the latest Cook ratings, Kansas moved from "Likely Republican" to "Lean Republican." South Carolina shifted from "Solid Republican" to "Likely Republican." Georgia and the seat held by Sen. Jon Ossoff (D) changed from "Lean Democrat" to "Likely Democrat." By the numbers: There are six Republican-held Senate seats rated by Cook as a "Toss Up" or better for Democrats. The Georgia shift makes a Republican pickup there less likely, while the Kansas move expands the map of competitive seats for Democrats. Zoom out: The midterms environment is improving for Democrats amid voter discontent about gas prices, the cost of living and the broader handling of the Iran war. Flashback: Last month, Cook shifted Senate and gubernatorial races in Texas and Iowa in Democrats' favor.

articles.summary: A truck driver hauling metal pipes made a right-hand turn in Topeka, Kansas, in February 2021, causing the heavy equipment to slide off the semi-trailer, slam into five vehicles and another truck, and kill one person. It was later revealed that the driver had an expired medical certificate and lacked the required record of duty status. The truck was also missing an up-to-date annual inspection and had several load-securement violations. A month before the crash, inspectors conducted a “remote” investigation of the trucking company, meaning they never visited the actual business and instead reviewed its documents virtually. Investigators closed the probe after a quick phone call with the company. Such “virtual” inspections were the standard at the time. During the earlier audit, the trucking company noted that the driver later involved in the tragic event was not employed by them, but said they kept him on the books because he would work for them on occasion.
